title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 2.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the LORD
Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre
Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men
The house which I build is great
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in the chapter as stated in 2 Chronicles 2:1.

questions.question: How many men did Solomon tell out to bear burdens?
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in 2 Chronicles 2:2.

questions.question: To whom did Solomon send a message for assistance?
options: King David
King Huram of Tyre
King Solomon
King Saul
questions.correctAnswer: King Huram of Tyre
questions.explanation: Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 2:3.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the house that Solomon intends to build?
options: To store treasures
To dedicate it to the LORD
To serve as a palace
To build a fortress
questions.correctAnswer: To dedicate it to the LORD
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Chronicles 2:4, where it mentions building an house to the name of the LORD my God.

questions.question: What does Solomon plan to burn before the LORD in the house?
options: Wood
Sweet incense
Oil
Grain
questions.correctAnswer: Sweet incense
questions.explanation: The text specifies that sweet incense is to be burned before the LORD as per 2 Chronicles 2:4.

questions.question: How often does Solomon intend to offer burnt offerings?
options: Daily
Weekly
Monthly
Morning and evening
questions.correctAnswer: Morning and evening
questions.explanation: This is clearly stated in 2 Chronicles 2:4, which mentions burnt offerings morning and evening.

questions.question: What does Solomon say about the greatness of God?
options: He is above all gods
He is invisible
He is a fortress
He is a warrior
questions.correctAnswer: He is above all gods
questions.explanation: Solomon states in 2 Chronicles 2:5 that great is our God above all gods.

questions.question: What does Solomon ponder about building a house for God?
options: Who can build Him a house?
What materials are needed?
Where should it be located?
How long will it take?
questions.correctAnswer: Who can build Him a house?
questions.explanation: This question is raised by Solomon in 2 Chronicles 2:6, emphasizing the vastness of God.

questions.question: What does Solomon acknowledge about the heavens?
options: They cannot contain God
They are beautiful
They are distant
They are empty
questions.correctAnswer: They cannot contain God
questions.explanation: Solomon acknowledges in 2 Chronicles 2:6 that the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him.

questions.question: How many men did Solomon assign to oversee the workers?
questions.explanation: This number is specified in 2 Chronicles 2:2 for those overseeing the workers.

questions.question: What is the reason Solomon gives for building the house?
options: To glorify himself
To fulfill a promise
To dedicate it to the LORD
To gain favor with Huram
questions.correctAnswer: To dedicate it to the LORD
questions.explanation: This is found in 2 Chronicles 2:4, highlighting the dedication of the house to God.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon determined to build a house for his kingdom.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the LORD and an house for his kingdom as stated in 2 Chronicles 2:1.

questions.question: True or False: The house Solomon builds is described as small.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Solomon declares that the house which he builds is great, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 2:5.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon intended to offer sacrifices only on the new moons.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Solomon intended to offer sacrifices on the sabbaths, new moons, and solemn feasts, as stated in 2 Chronicles 2:4.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon thought he was unworthy to build a house for God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: While Solomon questions who is able to build a house for God, he does not express unworthiness; he simply states the vastness of God in 2 Chronicles 2:6.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What specific skill does Solomon request in the man he asks to be sent to him in 2 Chronicles 2:7?
options: Cunning to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, purple, crimson, and blue, including skill to engrave
Skill to build houses and cut timber
Ability to lead men in battle
Expertise in writing and teaching the law
questions.correctAnswer: Cunning to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, purple, crimson, and blue, including skill to engrave
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:7 states Solomon asked for a man cunning to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, purple, crimson, and blue, and skilled to engrave with the cunning men in Judah and Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 2:9 promise will happen if Solomon's servants work with the servants of Huram as commanded in 2 Chronicles 2:8?
options: The house Solomon is about to build shall be wonderfully great
The kingdom of Judah will be enlarged
The people will receive abundant harvests
The temple will be finished in one year
questions.correctAnswer: The house Solomon is about to build shall be wonderfully great
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:9 promises that if Solomon's servants work with Huram's servants to prepare timber in abundance, the house Solomon is about to build will be wonderfully great.

questions.question: What types of trees does Solomon request from Lebanon to build the house as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 2:8?
options: Cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees
Oak trees, palm trees, and olive trees
Sycamore trees, fig trees, and pomegranate trees
Pine trees, cypress trees, and maple trees
questions.correctAnswer: Cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:8 records Solomon's request for cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees out of Lebanon for building the house.

questions.question: How does Huram the king of Tyre acknowledge Solomon’s authority and relationship with God in 2 Chronicles 2:11-12?
options: He recognizes that the LORD has loved His people and made Solomon king, and blesses God for giving David a wise son
He questions Solomon’s right to build the house and demands tribute
He offers to send soldiers to protect Solomon’s kingdom
He expresses doubt about Solomon’s wisdom and requests payment
questions.correctAnswer: He recognizes that the LORD has loved His people and made Solomon king, and blesses God for giving David a wise son
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:11-12 shows Huram acknowledging that the LORD has loved His people and made Solomon king, and blessing God for giving David a wise son endowed with understanding.

questions.question: What does Solomon offer to Huram’s servants who cut timber as described in 2 Chronicles 2:10?
options: Twenty thousand measures of wheat, barley, wine, and oil each
Ten thousand gold coins
Free land in Jerusalem
A share in the kingdom’s profits
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty thousand measures of wheat, barley, wine, and oil each
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:10 explains Solomon’s offer of twenty thousand measures each of wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the servants who cut timber for him.

questions.question: Why did Solomon say he was building the house for the LORD in 2 Chronicles 2:4?
options: To dedicate it to God and to burn incense and offerings continually according to ordinance
To display the wealth of Israel to other nations
To establish a royal palace for himself
To create a meeting place for the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To dedicate it to God and to burn incense and offerings continually according to ordinance
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:4 states Solomon’s purpose to build the house to dedicate it to the LORD, burning incense and offerings continually as an ordinance forever to Israel.

questions.question: How many men did Solomon assign to bear burdens and hew in the mountain according to 2 Chronicles 2:2?
options: Seventy thousand to bear burdens and eighty thousand to hew in the mountain
Ten thousand to bear burdens and five thousand to hew
One hundred thousand to bear burdens only
Thirty thousand to hew in the mountain only
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy thousand to bear burdens and eighty thousand to hew in the mountain
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:2 reports Solomon told out seventy thousand men to bear burdens and eighty thousand to hew in the mountain.

questions.question: What reason does Solomon give in 2 Chronicles 2:6 for questioning his ability to build a house for the LORD?
options: Because heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, so who is he to build Him a house?
Because the people lacked resources
Because he feared opposition from neighboring kingdoms
Because he was not skilled in building
questions.correctAnswer: Because heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, so who is he to build Him a house?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:6 reveals Solomon’s humility, recognizing that God is too great for any house as heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him.

questions.question: What does Solomon mean by saying the house he is building is great in 2 Chronicles 2:5?
options: It is great because God is greater than all other gods
It has more rooms than any palace
It will be the largest building in Jerusalem
It will be made of gold and silver
questions.correctAnswer: It is great because God is greater than all other gods
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:5 explains the greatness of the house is because God is great above all gods, emphasizing the honor due to Him.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 2:3, why did Solomon send to Huram king of Tyre?
options: Because Huram had dealt well with David by sending cedars to build his house
To request soldiers for battle
To ask for silver and gold
To invite Huram to visit Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Because Huram had dealt well with David by sending cedars to build his house
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:3 shows Solomon sent to Huram because Huram had previously sent cedars to David for building his house, seeking the same favor.

questions.question: What does Solomon’s request for skilled workers and abundant timber suggest about his approach to building the house?
options: He values quality craftsmanship and sufficient resources to create a magnificent temple
He is in a hurry and wants to finish quickly
He prefers to use local materials only
He wants to build a small, simple structure
questions.correctAnswer: He values quality craftsmanship and sufficient resources to create a magnificent temple
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:7-9 indicate Solomon’s desire for skilled artisans and abundant timber to ensure the temple is wonderfully great, showing dedication to excellence.

questions.question: How can Christians apply Solomon’s example of requesting skilled workers for building God’s house today?
options: By seeking God’s help to find gifted people for ministry and service
By doing everything alone without help
By focusing only on material wealth
By ignoring God’s instructions
questions.correctAnswer: By seeking God’s help to find gifted people for ministry and service
questions.explanation: Solomon’s dependence on skilled workers (2 Chronicles 2:7) shows the importance of recognizing and using God-given talents in the church community.

questions.question: What does Huram’s blessing of Solomon in 2 Chronicles 2:12 teach about recognizing God’s work in others?
options: We should praise God for wisdom and understanding given to leaders
We should criticize leaders for their faults
We should ignore God’s involvement in leadership
We should rely only on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: We should praise God for wisdom and understanding given to leaders
questions.explanation: Huram’s blessing (2 Chronicles 2:12) acknowledges God’s role in giving Solomon wisdom, encouraging believers to honor God’s work in leaders.

questions.question: Why does Solomon mention the continual burnt offerings and shewbread in 2 Chronicles 2:4?
options: To emphasize the temple’s role in ongoing worship and obedience to God
To suggest the offerings are optional
To highlight the temple as a royal residence
To show that sacrifices will be rare
questions.correctAnswer: To emphasize the temple’s role in ongoing worship and obedience to God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:4 describes the temple as a place for continual offerings, underscoring faithful worship as a lasting ordinance.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon requested the same kind of skilled workers that his father David had provided to build the temple.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:7 states Solomon asked for a man with skill to work alongside the skilled men David his father provided, showing continuity in skilled labor.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who did Huram send to Solomon as a skilled craftsman according to 2 Chronicles 2:13?
options: A cunning man, endued with understanding
A prophet to guide the work
A chief architect from Jerusalem
A warrior from Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: A cunning man, endued with understanding
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:13 states explicitly that Huram sent a cunning man endued with understanding to Solomon.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 2:14, what materials was the skilled craftsman from Tyre proficient in working with?
options: Gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson
Only gold and silver
Bronze and wood exclusively
Iron and stone only
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Chronicles 2:14 lists all these materials as those the craftsman was skillful in working with.

questions.question: What was Solomon's instruction regarding wheat, barley, oil, and wine in 2 Chronicles 2:15?
options: To send them to Huram's servants
To keep them for the temple offerings only
To distribute them among the Levites
To store them in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: To send them to Huram's servants
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:15 instructs Solomon to send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine to Huram's servants as part of their agreement.

questions.question: How was the timber from Lebanon delivered to Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 2:16?
options: In floats by sea to Joppa, then carried up to Jerusalem
By caravans overland from Lebanon
By direct shipment to Jerusalem port
By airlift through divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: In floats by sea to Joppa, then carried up to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:16 explains that wood was cut in Lebanon, floated by sea to Joppa, and then carried to Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 2:17, how many strangers did Solomon number in the land of Israel?
options: One hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred
Forty thousand
Seventy thousand
Two hundred thousand
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred
questions.explanation: The exact number of strangers Solomon counted is given in 2 Chronicles 2:17 as 150,000 plus 3,600.

questions.question: How did Solomon organize the laborers among the strangers according to 2 Chronicles 2:18?
options: Seventy thousand bearers of burdens, eighty thousand hewers in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers
All were set as hewers in the mountain
Half were overseers and half laborers
They were not organized but worked freely
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy thousand bearers of burdens, eighty thousand hewers in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:18 details Solomon's organization of laborers into three groups with specified numbers and roles.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'חָכָם' (chakam) in 2 Chronicles 2:13 mean?
options: Wise, skilled, or cunning
Prophet
King
Servant
questions.correctAnswer: Wise, skilled, or cunning
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'חָכָם' (chakam) used in 2 Chronicles 2:13 means wise or skilled, often translated as cunning in craftsmanship contexts.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 2:7 to 2 Chronicles 2:9 where Solomon requests materials and skilled workers from Huram?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with requests
Allegory, symbolic representation of spiritual truths
Parable, a short moral story
Hyperbole, exaggerated statements
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the narrative with requests
questions.explanation: The passage uses inclusio by framing Solomon's requests for workers and materials, emphasizing the preparation theme (2 Chronicles 2:7-9).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Solomon building the temple as a foreshadowing of Christ's spiritual temple?
options: Matthew 5:1-12
Acts 2:1-4
Revelation 21:1-4
questions.explanation: John 2:19-21 refers to Jesus speaking about destroying and raising the temple in three days, echoing Solomon's temple as a type of the body of Christ (2 Chronicles 2:1-3).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of skilled craftsmen working on the temple as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 2:13-14?
options: Exodus 31:1-6
Genesis 1:1-5
Leviticus 10:1-3
Numbers 20:1-13
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 31:1-6
questions.explanation: Exodus 31:1-6 describes Bezalel, filled with the Spirit of God, skilled in craftsmanship, paralleling the skilled workmen in 2 Chronicles 2:13-14.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Solomon sending a request to Huram, king of Tyre, in 2 Chronicles 2:3?
options: Solomon determining to build a house for the LORD and his kingdom
The numbering of strangers in Israel
Huram sending a skilled craftsman
Solomon offering sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon determining to build a house for the LORD and his kingdom
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:1-2 describe Solomon's decision to build the house before he sends the request in 2:3.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the detailed enumeration of laborers and materials in 2 Chronicles 2:2 and 2 Chronicles 2:10?
options: Parallelism emphasizing order and preparation
Irony, contrasting expectations
Metaphor for spiritual labor
Simile comparing workers to animals
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism emphasizing order and preparation
questions.explanation: The listing of laborers and materials shows parallelism stressing meticulous organization (2 Chronicles 2:2, 10).

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 2:6 reflect a theological humility in Solomon's approach to building the temple?
options: Solomon acknowledges God's transcendence and limits himself to offering sacrifices
Solomon claims he can contain God within the temple
Solomon boasts about his power to build the temple
Solomon refuses to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon acknowledges God's transcendence and limits himself to offering sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verse 6 expresses humility, recognizing heaven cannot contain God, and Solomon's role is to offer sacrifices.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 2:18, Solomon appointed exactly 3,600 overseers to direct the laborers.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:18 clearly states Solomon set 3,600 overseers to organize the people at work.

questions.question: True or False: Huram the king of Tyre refused to send cedar trees to Solomon for the temple construction.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:8 and 2 Chronicles 2:16 show that Huram agreed to cut and send cedar trees from Lebanon to Solomon.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 2:6 teach about God's transcendence and immanence?
options: God transcends all creation and cannot be contained, yet He allows Himself to be worshiped through the temple
God is limited by the physical universe and requires a temple to dwell among His people
God is only present in the temple and nowhere else
God’s presence is identical with the heavens, implying pantheism
questions.correctAnswer: God transcends all creation and cannot be contained, yet He allows Himself to be worshiped through the temple
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:6 states that the heavens cannot contain God, highlighting His transcendence, yet Solomon builds a temple to burn sacrifices before Him, demonstrating God's willingness to relate to humanity in a particular place.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine election and wisdom does 2 Chronicles 2:12 teach?
options: God’s love for His people results in bestowing wisdom and understanding to chosen leaders
Human wisdom alone accomplishes great works without divine aid
God’s election is random and unrelated to wisdom
Solomon’s wisdom was a natural inheritance without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God’s love for His people results in bestowing wisdom and understanding to chosen leaders
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:12 shows Huram attributing Solomon’s wisdom and prudence to the LORD’s love for Israel and His blessing on David’s son, indicating divine election and empowerment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the continuity of worship does 2 Chronicles 2:4 emphasize?
options: The temple worship, including incense, shewbread, and burnt offerings, is ordained forever as an enduring covenantal practice
Temple worship is temporary and will soon be obsolete
Worship is only individual and not corporate or institutional
Sacrificial worship is symbolic and not required for covenant relationship
questions.correctAnswer: The temple worship, including incense, shewbread, and burnt offerings, is ordained forever as an enduring covenantal practice
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:4 declares that the temple rituals are an ordinance forever to Israel, emphasizing the permanence of divinely appointed worship forms.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 2:5 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omnipresence
Justice
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:5 acknowledges God as great above all gods, highlighting His sovereign rule over all powers and authorities.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is clearly demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 2:11?
options: Covenant faithfulness
Wrath
Immanence
Omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:11 shows Huram recognizing the LORD’s love for His people and His establishment of Solomon as king, reflecting God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: How does Solomon’s building project in 2 Chronicles 2 prepare for the Messianic temple theme in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates the ultimate temple in Christ, who embodies God’s presence fully and permanently
It proves that physical temples are unnecessary for worship
It contradicts later Christian teaching about the temple
It shows that God’s presence is limited to physical structures
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the ultimate temple in Christ, who embodies God’s presence fully and permanently
questions.explanation: The temple Solomon builds is a type pointing to Christ as the true temple (John 2:19-21), fulfilling God’s presence among His people beyond a physical building.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 2:16 make regarding God’s provision and covenant with Israel?
options: God provides resources through Gentile cooperation, showing His plan to bless all nations
God’s covenant is exclusive and independent of others
Only Israel can supply materials for the temple
God’s provision is limited to Israel’s own resources
questions.correctAnswer: God provides resources through Gentile cooperation, showing His plan to bless all nations
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:16 describes wood being cut in Lebanon and brought to Jerusalem, illustrating how God uses Gentile nations like Tyre in His covenantal provision for Israel.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 2:1 and 2 Chronicles 2:6 teach about God’s relationship to His temple and human worship?
options: God is transcendent and cannot be contained, yet humans build a temple as a symbolic place for worship and sacrifice
God is confined to the temple and cannot be worshiped outside it
Human efforts can contain God fully through temple construction
God rejects temple worship because He is beyond it
questions.correctAnswer: God is transcendent and cannot be contained, yet humans build a temple as a symbolic place for worship and sacrifice
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Solomon’s intention to build a house for God, while verse 6 clarifies God’s transcendence beyond the heavens, underscoring the temple as a human-centered locus for worship without limiting God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine empowerment and human craftsmanship do 2 Chronicles 2:7 and 2 Chronicles 2:13 teach?
options: God endows gifted artisans with skill to carry out His purposes in temple construction
Human skill alone accomplishes temple work without divine blessing
Craftsmanship is unimportant for spiritual worship
Only Israelites can be skilled workers for God’s temple
questions.correctAnswer: God endows gifted artisans with skill to carry out His purposes in temple construction
questions.explanation: Verse 7 requests a skilled craftsman, and verse 13 shows Huram sending a gifted artisan, indicating divine providence enabling human skill for sacred tasks.

questions.question: What combined theological truth about God’s provision and covenantal blessing is taught by 2 Chronicles 2:10 and 2 Chronicles 2:15?
options: God’s covenant blessings include material provision for those serving His purposes
Sacrificial gifts are unnecessary for God’s blessing
God’s provision is only spiritual and never material
God’s blessings are independent of human cooperation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant blessings include material provision for those serving His purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 10 shows Solomon offering food and drink to workers, and verse 15 urges sending those provisions, illustrating God’s blessing through material support for His temple workers.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 2:17-18 exaggerates the number of foreigners in Israel to justify forced labor. What does these verses actually teach?
options: They report a large population of foreigners involved in temple labor, showing God’s providential use of all peoples
They justify exploitation of foreigners as slaves without divine sanction
They minimize the role of foreigners in Israel’s society
They teach that only Israelites built the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They report a large population of foreigners involved in temple labor, showing God’s providential use of all peoples
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:17-18 enumerates foreigners set to work under overseers, demonstrating God’s sovereign arrangement to use diverse peoples for His covenantal purposes.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s covenant faithfulness is taught by 2 Chronicles 2:3?
options: God’s covenant promises extend from David to Solomon, ensuring continuity in His redemptive plan
God’s covenant ended with David and does not include Solomon
Covenant promises require no human participation
God’s promises are conditional only on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant promises extend from David to Solomon, ensuring continuity in His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:3 references the dealings God had with David now continuing with Solomon, showing covenantal continuity across generations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 2:14 regarding the artisan sent by Huram?
options: Wisdom
Wrath
Jealousy
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:14 highlights the artisan’s cunning and skill, reflecting God’s attribute of wisdom bestowed on His servants for accomplishing His purposes.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 2:8 relate to the doctrine of God’s providential ordering of creation and nations?
options: By requesting timber from Lebanon, Solomon acknowledges God’s arrangement of nations to serve His purposes
The request ignores God’s sovereignty over nature
Only Israel can provide for its own needs independently
God’s providence excludes Gentile nations
questions.correctAnswer: By requesting timber from Lebanon, Solomon acknowledges God’s arrangement of nations to serve His purposes
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 2:8 shows Solomon relying on skilled workers and resources from Lebanon, demonstrating God’s providential use of Gentile nations in His covenant plan.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about human stewardship and divine blessing is taught by 2 Chronicles 2:2 and 2 Chronicles 2:18?
options: God blesses and organizes human labor for His holy purposes with both Israelites and foreigners under wise supervision
Human labor is irrelevant to divine plans
Only Israelite laborers are blessed by God
Divine blessing is independent of human order or stewardship
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses and organizes human labor for His holy purposes with both Israelites and foreigners under wise supervision
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 18 enumerate the large workforce including foreigners overseen by leaders, showing God’s providential ordering of labor for temple construction.
